newsitem.title: PERU: Explosion in Lima was mere science fiction.
newsitem.headline: Explosion in Lima was mere science fiction.

text.p: An explosion on Tuesday near the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima alarmed reporters but turned out to be no more than fireworks by a crew filming an American science fiction movie, police said.

A local production crew making the film "Volcano Run" said the blast, about a mile (1.6 km) from the residence where leftist rebels are holding 72 people hostage, was a "controlled explosion" that had been cleared with police.
It was not controlled enough for people living nearby, however, some of whose windows were blown out by the explosion underneath a car, police said.
"It affected about a three-block area. Supposedly it was a controlled explosion but people have been calling us to complain that their windows were blown out," a police spokesman said.
The blast, in Lima's Magdalena district, was too far away to be heard at the residence itself but local television quickly reported it and a few journalists rushed to the scene.

A spokewoman for the production company, Iguana Producciones, said the bomb was part of the plot of the film, which she described as a science fiction tale starring F. Murray Abraham and directed by Gwyneth Gibby.
Iguana will pay for the damages, she said.
